Border
BōR-d'r
n. (rendering Hebrew g'būl and qātseh, Greek horion)
From Old French bordure, an edge or brim, from a Frankish root meaning board or side. The Hebrew g'būl is stronger than the English suggests: it means not merely an edge but a bound set, a limit fixed by authority, and the same word does duty for the boundary of a field, the frontier of a nation, and the shore that bounds the sea. Behind every biblical border stands the One who set it.

Biblical Definition

A border in Scripture is a divine appointment before it is a human survey. The inheritance of each tribe was allotted by lot before the LORD, and its borders were therefore not negotiable lines but sacred trusts, which is why removing one was a covenant crime and not merely a property dispute: “Thou shalt not remove thy neighbour's landmark, which they of old time have set in thine inheritance” (Deu 19:14). Proverbs repeats it as a maxim of the wise: “Remove not the ancient landmark, which thy fathers have set” (Pro 22:28). The stone in the ground stood for something no man had the right to move, and a nation that begins moving its stones has begun dissolving. Because the borders are God's, He is free to enlarge them, and He promises to do so precisely when His people are most exposed by obedience: “For I will cast out the nations before thee, and enlarge thy borders: neither shall any man desire thy land, when thou shalt go up to appear before the LORD thy God thrice in the year” (Exo 34:24) — the men leave the frontier undefended three times a year to worship, and God undertakes the defence Himself. And peace within the borders is His gift, not the achievement of statecraft: “He maketh peace in thy borders, and filleth thee with the finest of the wheat” (Psa 147:14). God fixes bounds, God enlarges them, God keeps them.

Webster 1828 Definition

The outer edge or extremity of anything; the boundary or frontier of a territory; the ancient landmark set by the fathers, which Scripture forbids to remove; and the ornamental hem or fringe of a garment.

expand to see more

BORDER, n. 1. The outer edge of any thing; the brim, margin, or extremity.

2. The exterior limit of a country, province, or estate; the confine or frontier; as, the borders of a kingdom.

3. A boundary mark; the landmark set of old time in an inheritance. Deut. 19.

4. The hem, fringe, or ornamental edge of a garment; as the border of his garment, which the woman touched. Matt. 9.

5. In Scripture, the bounds of a people's habitation, appointed by God. He hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation. Acts 17.

Key Scripture

Deuteronomy 19:14 — "Thou shalt not remove thy neighbour's landmark, which they of old time have set in thine inheritance, which thou shalt inherit in the land that the LORD thy God giveth thee to possess it."

Proverbs 22:28 — "Remove not the ancient landmark, which thy fathers have set."

Exodus 34:24 — "For I will cast out the nations before thee, and enlarge thy borders: neither shall any man desire thy land, when thou shalt go up to appear before the LORD thy God thrice in the year."

Psalm 147:14 — "He maketh peace in thy borders, and filleth thee with the finest of the wheat."

Modern Corruption

Every boundary is treated as an arbitrary construction of power to be dissolved, so that limits of nation, property, office, and sex are all read as oppression rather than as the fixed appointments of a wise Creator.

expand to see more

The modern instinct is that a border is a wound. Because some borders have been drawn unjustly — and some certainly have — it is inferred that boundedness itself is the injustice, and the moral energy of an age goes into erasure. Scripture's testimony runs the other way: God determined the times before appointed and the bounds of men's habitation, and He did it so that they should seek the Lord. The limit is an instrument of mercy. The same God who set the shore against the sea — hitherto shalt thou come, but no further — sets bounds to nations, to households, to offices, and to the creational distinction of male and female, and in every case the bound is what makes the thing inside it able to flourish. A field without edges is not a larger field; it is not a field at all.

The corruption has a second and quieter form: not the dissolving of borders by ideology but the moving of them by greed. Thou shalt not remove thy neighbour's landmark is aimed at the strong man who shifts a stone by a foot each year, and the prophets name it among the sins that bring judgment — the princes of Judah were like them that remove the bound. It is the sin of encroachment, and it is respectable because it is gradual. It applies wherever appointed limits are quietly annexed: a magistrate absorbing the authority of the family, a church annexing the conscience Scripture leaves free, an employer taking the day God reserved. Recovering the border means recovering the fear of God in small increments, since it is by small increments that landmarks move.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew g'būl is a bound, boundary, or territory, and by metonymy the land enclosed; qātseh is an extremity or end. Greek horion is a boundary or coast, and gives the verb horizō, to mark off or determine.

expand to see more

Hebrew g'būl (H1366) — boundary, border, territory; the fixed limit of an inheritance, and by extension the inheritance itself.

Hebrew g'būlāh (H1367) — a bound or landmark, the feminine form used of the borders of the tribes in Joshua.

Hebrew qātseh (H7097) — end, extremity, uttermost part; from the uttermost part of heaven unto the other.

Greek horion (G3725) — a boundary, and in the plural the coasts or borders of a region; the coasts of Tyre and Sidon (Mat 15:21).

Greek horizō (G3724) — to mark out by bounds, to determine or appoint; used of God determining the bounds of men's habitation (Act 17:26).

Usage

"Of the landmark that may not be moved: thou shalt not remove thy neighbour's landmark (Deu 19:14; Pro 22:28)."

"Of borders enlarged by God: I will cast out the nations before thee, and enlarge thy borders (Exo 34:24)."

"Of peace within the borders as God's gift: he maketh peace in thy borders (Psa 147:14)."
